composers_checked.name: Vanhal, Johann Baptist
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music track lists: Op. 6 complete (Eybler) and the Kubin, Lotus, Stamic, Camesina and Bennewitz quartet discs; Op. 7 complete (Hyperion) and Nos. 2, 3, 6 on Naxos; Op. 20 trios Nos. 1-3 (Cesky rozhlas). MusicBrainz holds almost no Vanhal chamber recordings. Gap check against the de.wikipedia and klassika.info work lists (selections; no complete public list exists) and the recordings found: added Op. 1 Nos. 3-4, Op. 2 No. 3 and Op. 33 No. 3 quartets, the three Op. 40 piano quartets and a trio sonata.

note: Vanhal (c18): 1) Accompanied keyboard sonatas with all strings ad lib. in the first edition, kept under the brief's rule because they are recorded with the strings: the three Op. 12 quintets (Spányi, Authentic Quartet, Hungaroton 2009; source pages seen only as search results, as AllMusic and Presto refuse scripts) and an F minor 'Op. 1' trio (Aestas Musica, Aulos 2015) whose key is not among the six of André's Op. 1 on IMSLP (C, F, B-flat, E-flat, G, A), so it has no IMSLP page and low confidence. The rest of Op. 1 is skipped as 'keyboard sonata, strings ad lib.'; Op. 5 and the Sonata facile stay skipped as duos (one obbligato string part). 2) Not added for lack of identification: a 'Quartet for clarinet and string trio' on Centaur CRC 3055 (Crusell Quartet, 17:17, per AllMusic; key not found) and one unnumbered Op. 17 trio on a Nota Bene EP. klassika.info also lists a String Quartet in G major, Op. 4 No. 1 and 'Op. 13a Nos. 1-6' that could not be matched to a recording. 3) Op. 40 piano quartets: the only recording (Richard Fuller, Musica Aeterna Bratislava) is sold by the pianist; label, year and timings not found. 4) Catalogue numbers: IMSLP calls Op. 6 No. 1 'Bryan F6' where the Kubin disc says 'F14', so opus-only titles there; IMSLP's 'Bryan A4' for Op. 33 No. 2 is Weinmann Va:A4 on the cpo disc. Opus numbers of Op. 1, Op. 2 and the 'Op. 3' trio sonata are as on the recordings. Minutes are medians of the recordings; Hyperion's Op. 7 timings run well below Naxos's (repeats). Levels are estimates without score inspection.
